chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:

When virtue dominates the era and its people, and a man suspects another man of evil from whom no evil has appeared, he has been unjust. And when vice dominates the era and its people, and a man has good opinion of another man, he has been deceived.

key_terms.حَوْبَةٌ: Evil, harm, or a visible flaw
key_terms.غَرَّرَ: He was deceived or led into peril

ai.seo_question: How should one balance suspicion and trust based on the moral state of the times?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) establishes a dynamic framework for social judgment, linking the virtue of suspicion or trust to the prevailing moral climate of the era. This principle, central to Shia ethical jurisprudence, warns that in times of general righteousness, baseless doubt constitutes an injustice (zulm), whereas in eras of corruption, uncritical trust leads to self-deception (gharar).
